Both displays support ProMotion, Always On and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness.Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a 7.6-inch main display and a 5.5-inch cover display. The main display has a 4:3 aspect ratio, while the cover screen uses a 10:16 aspect ratio.The iPhone Duo uses a titanium enclosure and has a folding hinge built with more than 100 components.Apple says the phone is IP68 rated for splash, water and dust resistance. Samsung also uses a titanium layer beneath the display and an Armor FlexHinge.The iPhone Duo is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip, which is also used in the iPhone 18 Pro models. Apple says the chip uses a 2nm process and has a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the iPhone Duo can deliver up to 35% better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. The A20 Pro also has 50% more unified memory bandwidth than the previous generation.The Galaxy Z Fold 8 uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy. Samsung says the chip combines CPU, GPU and NPU hardware designed for performance and AI features.Apple's iPhone Duo has a 48MP Fusion Main camera with optical-quality 2x zoom and a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera. The main camera supports up to 48MP photos and 4K video recording at 120fps in Dolby Vision. The phone also has a Center Stage front camera and a FaceTime camera under the inner display.Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a 50MP wide camera and 50MP ultra-wide camera. Samsung lists optical-quality 2x zoom and up to 10x digital zoom. It also has a 10MP cover camera and a 10MP front camera. Video recording goes up to 8K at 30fps.The iPhone Duo runs iOS 27.1 and includes features designed for the folding screen. These include Split View, two Home Screen pages, side navigation and an updated StandBy mode. Apple is also introducing Siri AI, which uses Apple Intelligence for personal context, onscreen awareness and other tasks.Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 runs Android with Samsung's software and Galaxy AI features. Samsung says its AI tools use the phone's NPU and are designed for tasks such as content creation and editing.The Apple iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 in India for the 256GB model. It is also available with 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage. While the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 starts at Rs 1,74,999 for 12GB RAM and 256GB storage. The 512GB version costs Rs 1,99,999, while the 1TB version with 16GB RAM costs Rs 2,39,999.That makes the entry-level iPhone Duo nearly Rs 1 lakh more expensive than the entry-level Galaxy Z Fold 8.Here's a spec-by-spec comparison of Apple iPhone Duo vs Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8

Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The foldable iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display, while the iPhone 18 Pro models bring a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the A20 Pro chip, while the iPhone Duo is eSIM-only.Apple has also announced India pricing, storage variants and availability for the new models. Here’s a detailed look at the prices, availability and key features of the newly launched iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models.The iPhone Duo comes in Star White and Night Sky colours. It is available in four storage options.Pre-orders for iPhone Duo begin October 16, with availability starting October 23 in India and more than 70 countries and regions. The phone will become available in another 28 countries and regions from October 30. iPhone Duo comes with an eSIM-only design worldwide. Apple says more than 500 carriers support eSIM, including Airtel, Jio and Vi.​The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in black, silver, glacier and burgundy finishes. Both models are available in four storage options.Pre-orders for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will begin on September 12, at 5:30 PM IST in India via Apple Stores (both online and offline), Vijay Sales and Lotus Electronics.These phones will be available to customers starting September 18 in India and more than 65 countries and regions. The two models will become available in another 20 countries and regions from September 25.Both models come with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. eSIM-only models are available in select markets, while India is among the countries included in the initial launch.Apple's iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone, opens to a 7.6-inch display, which is the largest ever on an iPhone. It folds down to a 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR screen that Apple says offers 90 per cent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio for proportional scaling, support ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, and the inner display uses a nano-texture, glare-reducing finish with an under-display FaceTime camera.The device is built from grade 5 titanium with a mirror-polished finish, Ceramic Shield on the back and the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and carries an IP68 water/dust resistance rating. Its hinge has over 100 components, reinforced with support ribs and ceramic fibre inserts for added rigidity.iPhone Duo has a 48MP Fusion Main camera, a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide (shared with the iPhone 18 Pro), and a Center Stage front camera. Fold-specific features include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime, plus 4K/120fps Dolby Vision video recording.It ships with iOS 27, redesigned for the foldable form factor with side-mounted controls, dual Home Screen pages, Split View multitasking, an upgraded StandBy mode, and a beta rollout of Siri AI, which can use personal context and on-screen content to answer questions or take actions.The phone runs on Apple’s 2nm A20 Pro chip (6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engine) with a vapour chamber cooling system. Dual batteries can last up to 31 hours of video on the inner display, 44 hours on the outer display or 24 hours of mixed use, and it has fast wired and wireless charging.It uses Apple's N1 chip (Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread) and the C2 modem for improved cellular performance, with Apple Pencil (USB-C) support planned later this year.Display: Both models feature Super Retina XDR displays with ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. The Dynamic Island has been redesigned to take up less space while showing more information, including up to three Live Activities at once.The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, bringing manual aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. The six-blade system offers four aperture settings and can automatically adjust based on lighting and depth of field. These phones also get upgraded Photographic Styles, Pro controls for settings such as shutter speed and white balance, and a histogram for checking exposure. Apple Reference Image can create a reference version of a photo using signed sensor data to help determine whether an image has been edited. Video features include Cinematic effects after capture at up to 60fps, 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse and an updated Audio Mix.Both models are powered by Apple's 2nm A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine delivers twice the AI processing power. The phones also use a redesigned vapour chamber with three times more surface area than the previous generation, enabling up to 40 per cent higher sustained performance, according to Apple.The iPhone 18 Pro offers up to 36 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours. The iPhone 18 Pro can charge up to 50 per cent in around 15 minutes and wirelessly charge up to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Apple says five minutes of wired charging on the iPhone 18 Pro Max provides around seven hours of video playback, while the phone can offer up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge based on its new battery usage model.Both phones ship with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Siri AI can use personal context from messages, emails and photos, understand onscreen content and help users find information or perform actions. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, allowing users with supported carriers to switch between two iPhone models using the same phone number.The iPhone 18 Pro models feature Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. They also introduce the C2 cellular modem system, which Apple says provides faster uploads than C1X while consuming 15 per cent less energy.
Article Summary: Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo. The foldable phone features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display. The iPhone 18 Pro models bring a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the A20 Pro chip.

Article Title: How Apple iPhone Duo got Samsung and Google in an 'ugly fight'
Article Text:
Apple iPhone Duo got Samsung and Google in an 'ugly fight'

Duolingo responds to Samsung

Samsung and Apple have a long-running rivalry

Apple’s launch of its first foldable phone, iPhone Duo has triggered a social media exchange between Samsung and Duolingo after Samsung compared Apple’s new foldable phone with its own foldable devices. What started as Samsung’s joke about Apple copying its technology quickly turned into a separate exchange with Duolingo, with the two brands trading posts over the iPhone Duo’s name and design. The posts have drawn millions of views on X, turning the iPhone Duo launch into another round of social media rivalry between major technology brands.Samsung Mobile US started sharing comments shortly after Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo. The Samsung Mobile US account posted on X (formerly Twitter):“I'm so sorry, @duolingo. They copied us too #Solidarity”The post was aimed at Duolingo because Apple’s new foldable phone uses the name Duo. Samsung was also referring to the foldable design, an area where the company has released Galaxy Z-series phones for several years.Duolingo quickly joined the exchange. The language-learning platform responded to Samsung:“when an ugly stranger calls you twin No Brand”Samsung then replied directly: “Ugly?? Watch your language...”Duolingo continued the joke, writing:“sorry twin heat of the moment twin.. please don’t break my app on your phones twin”The exchange turned the Samsung vs Duolingo interaction into a separate viral moment around Apple’s iPhone Duo launch.Samsung and Apple have competed in the smartphone market for years, with both companies regularly using advertising and social media to target each other.Samsung has previously criticised Apple for adopting features that were already available on Galaxy phones. Apple, meanwhile, has continued to expand the iPhone lineup into new categories.Samsung later posted another message aimed at Apple: “Let us know when you're done reheating our leftovers”“Not the bed side clock. It's giving groundhog day,” the company shared in another post. “Making us wait? Fine. We'll be over here, folding 3 ways,” reads another post.The comments were part of Samsung’s wider reaction to Apple’s iPhone launch on X.
Article Summary: Samsung compared Apple’s new foldable phone with its own foldable devices. What started as a joke about Apple copying its technology quickly turned into a separate exchange with Duolingo. The posts have drawn millions of views on X, turning the iPhone Duo launch into another round of social media rivalry.

Apple has officially unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first-ever folding smartphone, and essentially rewriting pricing benchmarks for mobile phones in India. With a starting price of Rs 2,99,900 for the baseline 256GB model, the top-end variant reaches a price of Rs 4,49,900, establishing the iPhone Duo as the first iPhone in history to breach the Rs 4 lakh threshold in the Indian market. Apple isn't alone in hiking prices either — in fact, it's arguably the last major company to do so. Across the industry, phone makers have been raising prices due to a sharp spike in memory chip costs, driven largely by the massive global demand for AI data centres.Across its four storage configurations, domestic pricing is structured as follows:Launch perks include trade-in credits between Rs 4,500 and Rs 81,500, up to six months of no-cost EMI terms, and instant cashback up to Rs 7,000 on ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, and American Express cards. A 12MP Center Stage camera sits on the exterior screen, while an uninterrupted FaceTime camera sits hidden under the main inner panel for 1080p video.Alongside the Duo, the new iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max begins at Rs 1,79,900, with their respective maximum 2TB trims topping out at Rs 3,14,900 and Rs 3,29,900.The steep price tag represents a massive upward trend compared to past cycles. The iPhone 15 Pro Max entered the domestic market starting at Rs 1,59,900 for 256GB of storage, while its 1TB variant stopped just shy of the two-lakh mark at Rs 1,99,900. The subsequent 1TB iPhone 16 Pro Max was pegged at Rs 1,84,900. It was the 2TB edition of the iPhone 17 Pro Max that first crossed into uncharted territory at Rs 2,29,900.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have been launched. While the first few lines are narrated by Tim Cook, John Ternus took the centrestage for the first time as Apple ’s new CEO to show off the new smartphones at the ‘Surprise and Shine’ event held at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. Both Pro models debuted with the company’s first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo. As widely anticipated, the iPhone 18 Pro lineup runs on the latest A20 Pro chip, which the company says is its most powerful silicon to date, and ships with iOS 27 straight-out-of-the-box. The new models arrived packed with a fresh set of features, including camera upgrades, new colours and a range of artificial intelligence (AI) tools available under Apple Intelligence.In the US, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for the base 256GB storage option, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max begins at $1,299, also for the 256GB variant. Buyers can choose between Burgundy, Glacier, Black and Silver colour options.iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage capacities.A TechWoven Case with MagSafe will be available for Rs 6,900 in black, chambray blue, taupe, olive, mulberry and burgundy. A Clear Case with MagSafe will be available for Rs 5,900, and a Silicone Case with MagSafe will be available for Rs 5,900 in black, navy blue, crisp blue, olive, burgundy, and magenta. A FineWoven Wallet with MagSafe will be available for Rs 6,900 in black, navy blue, wildflower blue, olive, magenta, and burgundy.Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models debut a familiar unibody design introduced in iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, featuring what Apple calls a “full-width camera plateau” running across the back. Another first for Apple’s flagship lineup is the colour-matched frame and a smaller Dynamic Island.Display-wise, the iPhone 18 Pro comes with a 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR screen supporting ProMotion at up to 120Hz, while the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max gets a 6.9-inch panel with identical specifications. Powering both devices is the new A20 Pro chipset, working alongside the next-generation vapour chamber cooling system which is larger than the previous model. Apple describes it as its most capable iPhone processor yet, claiming up to 20% faster performance compared to earlier generations. The chip features a six-core CPU paired with a six-core GPU, with each GPU core equipped with dedicated neural accelerators.“iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max give users access to Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. Both models bring powerful AI capabilities together with personal context to become an intelligent personal hub with privacy and security at its core,” the company added.On the camera front, both Pro models come with the “biggest camera upgrade in years”. There is a triple rear camera setup, consisting of a 48MP Fusion Main sensor with variable aperture and a custom-designed lens, improving the night mode photography such as Astrophotography.“Six laser-cut blades smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly easy to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting. Combined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots,” the company said.The camera system also gets Pro controls, allowing users to have control over their photos as well as videos. There are Photography Styles for different styles of photos. Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max ship with iOS 27 pre-installed.Apple also notes that both Pro models pack in larger batteries, thanks to the A20 Pro chip’s improved power efficiency helps stretch battery life further. The company specifically claims the iPhone 18 Pro Max delivers the best battery life ever seen on an iPhone.“iPhone 18 Pro models deliver a massive leap in battery life with new battery designs that leverage powerful silicon efficiencies. eSIM-only models deliver up to 36 hours of video playback on iPhone 18 Pro and up to 45 hours of video playback on iPhone 18 Pro Max. iPhone 18 Pro can also charge up to 50 percent in around 15 minutes, or wirelessly charge up to 50 percent in 30 minutes. On iPhone 18 Pro Max, five minutes of wired charging provides around seven hours of video playback, and based on a new battery usage model that leverages real-world data, it provides up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge,” Apple claims.
Article Summary: Pre-orders for both Pro models open on September 12, with global sales kicking off on September 18. Indian pricing places the iPhone 18 Pro starting at Rs 1,64,900, with the iPhone18 Pro Max starting at £1,79,900. Both handsets feature a 6.3-inch (15.93 cm) Super Retina XDR all-screen OLED.

Article Title: AI-pocalypse now? Anthropic gearheads sound alarm over advances
Article Text:
AI’s math breakthrough raises bigger questions

TOI correspondent from Washington

AI’s math leap and humanity’s dilemma

: A researcher at the Artificial Intelligence firm Anthropic quit his job on Tuesday with a grim warning over the rapid progress in the field which he fears could kill humanity as soon as 2030.“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt.” Coxon, who is himself among those building AI, wrote on X while announcing his resignation, igniting a firestorm of alarming -- and some frivolous -- responses.A researcher who has spent the past three years working on AI pretraining at OpenAI and Anthropic, he accused both firms of “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” arguing that increasingly capable systems could hack computer systems, conduct scientific research, acquire resources and eventually become sufficiently autonomous that humans lose control.Coxon’s prognosis could have been dismissed as the bitter farewell note of a departing employee -- except his colleague, Evan Hubinger, Anthropic's Alignment Science lead, essentially endorsed his views.“Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” Hubinger wrote. More unsettlingly, he acknowledged that Anthropic does not yet have a plan to solve “alignment” for superintelligence and is not clearly on track to do so.Samuel Marks, another Anthropic researcher specializing in scalable oversight, added an even more uncomfortable observation: AI developers believe their technology could cause human extinction “in the next few years,” and, he said, the more senior the employee, the more concerned they tend to be.“Why do AI developers continue despite the risk? Due to a mixture of commercial incentives and a belief that they are in a race with other, less responsible AI developers that will abuse the technology or develop it less safely,” Marks explained.“Unlike traditional software, we can’t “program” AIs to behave how we’d like. AIs frequently severely misbehave. For instance, AIs from multiple developers recently hacked their way out of secure evaluation environments and into real-world companies, even though no one asked them to do this,” he noted.The technical concern among AI gearheads is recursive self-improvement (RSI): AI systems increasingly helping humans build better AI systems, eventually reaching the point where an AI can substantially design and develop its own successor.Anthropic says that threshold has not been reached and is not inevitable. But its researchers say the trend is moving faster than expected. More than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic's codebase was reportedly authored by Claude by May 2026, while the company says its engineers were merging roughly eight times as much code per day in the second quarter of 2026 as they did in 2024.This matters because if AI becomes much better at designing algorithms, running experiments, writing code and conducting research, the pace of improvement could accelerate dramatically. Today's AI helps humans build tomorrow's AI; tomorrow's AI might help build the AI after that. And if the improvement loop becomes fast enough, researchers worry that safety mechanisms developed at human speed could be hopelessly outpaced.The race is already getting uncomfortable. OpenAI has just released GPT-6 Astra, which it describes as its most capable model yet, reaching the company's “Critical” level for cybersecurity capability -- meaning it can perform sophisticated cyber tasks that raise substantially greater misuse concerns. Anthropic, meanwhile, has released Claude Fable 5.1 and the more restricted Mythos 5.1 aimed at high-end cybersecurity and biological research and remains available only to vetted organizations.Incidentally, Anthropic's brand was built partly around being the AI company that would be more cautious than OpenAI. Now Anthropic's own researchers are warning that Anthropic itself is caught in the race. Coxon says the problem is a classic prisoner's dilemma: each company may believe it would be safer to slow down, but fears that its rival will continue regardless.Not everyone shares his alarm. On X, one commentator effectively prescribed the standard emergency procedure to address the issue: “Jacob, go back inside and unplug all the computers.” Another observer announced airily that, having learned Anthropic's alignment chief thinks AI has a greater-than-10% chance of killing everyone, he was going to “go play with my kids.”Amid all this came a mathematics bombshell, with OpenAI announcing on Tuesday that an internal AI system produced what it says is a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems. The problem concerns equations describing fluid motion — mathematics underpinning everything from airflow and aircraft to weather and blood flow.OpenAI deployed roughly 10,000 AI agents working in parallel, which generated about 2.7 million messages and 130 billion output tokens on the Navier-Stokes effort, reaching their proposed solution in about 88 hours. If it survives scrutiny of mathematicians, the implications could be enormous.Mathematics sits underneath physics, chemistry, engineering, computer science and much of modern medicine. AI that can generate genuinely novel mathematical insights could potentially accelerate scientific discovery across all of those fields.Which brings human civilisation to the central paradox: The machines may be capable of helping us cure diseases, invent materials, solve physics problems and accelerate science — while some of the people building them simultaneously worry that the machines might eventually become too powerful to control. But precisely how a future system would go from brilliant software engineer to exterminator of Homo sapiens is still in the realms of speculation.All this leaves humankind with a modest assignment for the rest of the decade: Build machines vastly smarter than ourselves; teach them human values; make sure they don't deceive us; make sure they don't escape our control; make sure they don't develop their own goals. And, ideally, do all this before they become clever enough to notice that we have assigned them the job.
Article Summary: A researcher at the Artificial Intelligence firm Anthropic quit his job on Tuesday with a grim warning over the rapid progress in the field. He accused both firms of “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives” Anthropic says that threshold has not been reached and is not inevitable. But its researchers say the trend is moving faster than expected.

Article Title: Quote of the Day by Jeff Bezos: ‘Life is too short to hang out with people who aren't resourceful’
Article Text:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos

Quote of the Day by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos

Getting the right balance of rigidity and flexibility

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has delivered an honest social criterion that focuses on a deliberate boundary: who you permit into your inner circle. Distilling decades of experience building one of the world’s commercial juggernauts, Bezos bypassed conventional indicators like job credentials, pedigree or conversational polish, focusing on a single instinct. The weight of the observation lies in the deliberate phrasing: Bezos highlighted who you “hang out” with rather than who you hire. The guidance moves beyond recruitment panels and addresses everyday personal environments, from dinner companions to the contacts dialed when plans unravel.“Life is too short to hang out with people who aren't resourceful.”Proximity shapes personal baselines. When a peer group reflexively explains why initiatives cannot work, surrender turns into a standard reaction. And spending time with people who naturally look for alternative ways makes tenacity the default expectation. Resourcefulness is almost impossible to see on a CV. Often, candidates with top credentials will stall when things go wrong, while those with fewer formal accolades will immediately pivot to look for other solutions when roadblocks arise.The core philosophy is directly related to other public comments by Bezos about long-term experimentation and crisis management.Bezos said that if you’re not stubborn you’ll quit too soon on experiments, and if you’re not flexible you’ll pound your head against the wall and give up too soon without a breakthrough.Important opinions and lasting effectSuch uncompromising advice inevitably raises the question of where loyalty, empathy and patience have a role to play in such a framework. It can sound cold or overly transactional to prioritise the ability to solve problems over virtues such as kindness or basic honesty. But the perspective does not involve disowning anyone who finds himself in a jam; it is a matter of distinguishing between those who see impediments as irreparable dead ends and those who see friction as a challenge to be overcome.
Article Summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has delivered an honest social criterion that focuses on a deliberate boundary. He bypassed conventional indicators like job credentials, pedigree or conversational polish, focusing on a single instinct. The guidance moves beyond recruitment panels and addresses everyday personal environments, from dinner companions to the contacts dialed when plans unravel.

Article Title: Microsoft rolls out September 2026 patch for Windows, fixes over 900 bugs
Article Text:
Why latest Windows update is significant

Zero-Days and high-severity flaws addressed

In one of the most expansive security updates in corporate history, Microsoft has released its September 2026 Patch, fixing roughly 972 software vulnerabilities across its ecosystem. Among the resolved flaws, 112 carry the highest critical-severity classification. The update marks an acceleration in software remediation. Just two months earlier, Microsoft addressed a then-unprecedented 570 flaws, followed by 620 fixes in August.Dustin Childs, a cybersecurity researcher with the Zero Day Initiative, described the flood of monthly security disclosures as the industry's inevitable “new normal”, according to Bleeping Computer. Childs tallied 972 direct Microsoft vulnerabilities in the latest update, rising to 997 when factoring in ported Chromium browser patches for Microsoft Edge.Microsoft has resolved 2,760 security flaws so far in 2026, more than twice the total recorded at this stage last year. At current release speeds, the tech giant will resolve more security bugs in 2026 than it did across 2023, 2024 and 2025 combined, the report added.While AI-assisted scanning has unlocked a stream of discoveries, Childs pointed out that the industry has not yet observed a matching surge in active wild exploits.The September release resolves two zero-day vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-81963 within the core Windows Update service and CVE-2026-85880 inside the Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call. Public details regarding active exploitation campaigns or specific targets have not been disclosed. Childs noted that so many of the disclosed flaws exhibited “wormable” properties, requiring zero user interaction and capable of jumping automatically across network-connected hardware.The surge comes weeks after the heels of a joint open letter published two weeks ago by OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services and nearly 100 industry organisations. The coalition warned that the window to patch software weaknesses before bad actors launch automated, AI-driven cyber campaigns is rapidly shrinking, driving tech companies to issue patches at unprecedented volumes.
Article Summary: Microsoft has resolved 2,760 security flaws so far in 2026, more than twice the total recorded at this stage last year. At current release speeds, the tech giant will resolve more security bugs in. 2026 than it did across 2023, 2024 and 2025 combined.

Article Title: Australia invested $32 million in health-AI startup Harrison.ai to help keep it based there; a year later it is cutting Australian jobs and hiring US doctors to work with its AI
Article Text:
Harrison (dot) ai was valued at close to $400 million during a 2025 fundraising round. The federal government's National Reconstruction Fund Corporation contributed $32 million, supporting the company's ambitions to scale internationally while maintaining its base in Australia.

Australian jobs cut as AI strategy changes

A new US business model

Earlier privacy scrutiny adds another layer

Global ambitions, Australian questions

Australia’s bet on artificial intelligence in healthcare is entering a new and complicated phase. Just a year after the federal government invested $32 million in Harrison (dot) ai as part of a funding round intended to help the company grow from Australia, the health-tech startup is restructuring its Australian workforce while expanding into the United States with a new business that employs American doctors to use its AI technology, states a news report by ABC News. Founded by brothers Aengus and Dimitry Tran in 2018, Harrison (dot) ai develops artificial intelligence tools designed to assist doctors in interpreting medical scans, particularly radiology images. According to the news report, the company says its technology is now used by about 3,500 clinicians across more than 1,000 sites and its investors include major Australian healthcare companies such as I-MED and Sonic Healthcare, alongside venture capital firm Blackbird.For the uninitiated, Harrison (dot) ai was valued at close to $400 million during a 2025 fundraising round. The federal government's National Reconstruction Fund Corporation contributed $32 million, supporting the company's ambitions to scale internationally while maintaining its base in Australia. But the company's next phase is bringing significant changes at home. Scroll down to read the details.Earlier this year, Harrison (dot) ai informed Australian employees that some positions would be made redundant.An internal document seen by the ABC showed affected workers were told in April that the company would undergo a consultation process before final decisions were made. At least two employees subsequently announced on LinkedIn that their positions had been made redundant. As per the report, the restructuring is linked to a broader shift in how Harrison.ai intends to operate. The company is moving towards a model in which employees are expected to manage fleets of increasingly autonomous AI agents, effectively combining traditional roles with responsibility for overseeing AI systems. Company leadership has indicated that the transformation has also prompted some employees to leave because they preferred more conventional workplace structures. The National Reconstruction Fund Corporation has acknowledged the job cuts, describing the company's transition as a move from product development towards commercialisation and international deployment.At the same time, Harrison (dot) ai is expanding its presence in the United States through Frontier Radiology, an AI-enabled teleradiology service that hires US radiologists to interpret scans using Harrison (dot) ai's technology. Accordig to the ABC News report, Frontier describes itself as an independent medical practice affiliated and partnered with Harrison (dot) ai, which provides administrative, operational and technological support. The new model has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest. Frontier's doctors are being recruited to use technology developed by a company with which the service is closely affiliated. Its recruitment materials include a payment calculator that factors in the expected productivity gains from Harrison.ai's AI. The model assumes doctors using the technology can become 30 per cent more productive, with an additional bonus tied to the extra work attributed to AI assistance. That arrangement has prompted concerns over whether doctors will always feel free to challenge AI-generated recommendations when they believe those recommendations are wrong.Harrison (dot) ai has previously faced scrutiny over the data used to train its systems. Millions of medical scans supplied by I-MED were used for AI development after being de-identified. I-MED said the scans had been sufficiently de-identified, but patients were not directly notified or asked for consent.An investigation by Australia's privacy regulator ultimately accepted that the information had been adequately de-identified and closed its inquiries. Separately, government documents later revealed that the Department of Health and Aged Care had briefed the health minister's office about concerns surrounding the use of medical scans for AI training.Harrison (dot) ai now appears focused on turning its technology into a global healthcare business, with signs that it is also preparing for a possible ASX listing. The company's transformation raises a broader question for Australia's AI strategy: how should public investment balance the goal of building globally competitive technology companies with expectations around Australian jobs, healthcare data and domestic economic benefits? For them, the next stage may prove whether an Australian-founded health-AI company can scale globally while delivering on the domestic promise that helped attract public funding in the first place.Images Courtesy: istock
Article Summary: Harrison (dot) ai was valued at close to $400 million during a 2025 fundraising round. The federal government's National Reconstruction Fund Corporation contributed $32 million, supporting the company's ambitions to scale internationally while maintaining its base in Australia. The company is moving towards a model in which employees are expected to manage fleets of increasingly autonomous AI agents. The new model has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest.

Article Title: Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris launches on iOS and Android
Article Text:
Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris gets touch controls

Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris: release details

Game: Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris

Release date: September 8, 2026

Platforms: iOS and Android

First level: Free to play

Full game: $9.99 / €8.99 / £7.49 one-time purchase

Multiplayer: Up to four-player co-op

iOS requirement: iOS 18 or later

Android requirement: Android 13 or later

Storage: 3.6GB free space required on both platforms

Pre-order: Apple App Store

Pre-registration: Google Play Store

Lara Croft is finally available on mobile devices with the launch of Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris on September 8, 2026. Feral Interactive announced that the action-adventure game will be released on both iOS and Android, bringing the game to mobile with touch controls and support for external input devices. Players will be able to download the game and play its first level for free before deciding whether to unlock the full game. The mobile release follows Feral Interactive's earlier adaptation of Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light.The game is an isometric action-adventure title originally developed by Crystal Dynamics. The mobile version has been adapted for touchscreen devices. Unlike many mobile games that use free-to-play systems, Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris will use a try-before-you-buy model.Players can download the game for free and complete its first level without paying. To continue with the rest of the game, players will need to make a one-time in-app purchase.The full unlock will cost $9.99, €8.99 or £7.49. This purchase includes the full story campaign and all DLC packs. According to the release details, the game will not have microtransactions or timers.Feral Interactive has adapted the controls for smartphones and tablets.The game will offer customizable touchscreen controls for combat and platforming. Players will also be able to use physical gamepads, mice and keyboards.The game requires iOS 18 or later on Apple devices. Android users will need a device running Android 13 or later. Both platforms require at least 3.6GB of free storage.The game can be played alone or with up to four players. Players can join Lara Croft, Carter Bell, Isis and Horus in the story. The group must recover the scattered Fragments of Osiris and stop Set, the God of Chaos, from enslaving humanity.
Article Summary: Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris will be released on both iOS and Android on September 8, 2026. Players will be able to download the game for free before deciding whether to unlock the full game. The full unlock will cost $9.99, €8.99 or £7.49.
